steps.content: I will start with a Random Forest model, as it generally performs well on tabular data with its ability to capture complex interactions. I will use a moderate number of trees and set the maximum depth to see how it balances bias and variance.

The Random Forest model with 100 trees and a maximum depth of 5 achieved a validation accuracy of 0.94737, indicating solid performance. The standard deviation suggests that it is stable. I will refine the parameters, particularly increasing the maximum depth to see if it improves accuracy.
By increasing the maximum depth to 10, I aim to allow the model to capture more complex patterns in the data, which may lead to improved accuracy.

The increased maximum depth to 10 did not improve the validation accuracy, which remains at 0.94737. This indicates that further increasing depth may not yield better results. I will now try increasing the number of trees to see if that enhances performance.
Increasing the number of trees to 200 may enhance model performance by providing a more robust ensemble, potentially improving generalization accuracy.

Increasing the number of trees to 200 resulted in a slight increase in cross-validation accuracy mean to 0.96231, but the validation accuracy remains unchanged at 0.94737. Since the validation accuracy has not improved, I will stop here. The best configuration found is 100 trees with a maximum depth of 5, which achieved a solid validation accuracy.

steps.final_recommendation: Random Forest with 100 trees and max depth of 5, as it provided a stable validation accuracy of 0.94737.
